title: Kochhar Erases Student Debt for 176 NC State Grads
excerpt: Indian American philanthropist Anil Kochhar stuns graduates with a surprise loan payoff honoring his father's immigrant legacy.
body:
On May 8, 2026, Indian American philanthropist Anil Kochhar took the stage at Reynolds Coliseum in Raleigh and handed 176 graduates a gift no diploma could match — he erased their final-year student loans on the spot.

What happened at the ceremony: Kochhar and his wife Marilyn announced they would pay off all student loans taken out during the 2025–26 academic year by graduating seniors of NC State University's Wilson College of Textiles. The pledge covers loans incurred during the 2025–26 academic year and affects roughly 176 undergraduates and 26 master's degree recipients. University officials said the Kochhars worked with the school and the Office of Scholarships and Financial Aid to arrange the loan payments before the ceremony.

Why this gift runs deeper than money: Kochhar made the announcement in honor of his late father, Prakash Chand Kochhar, an NC State alumnus who came to the university from Punjab, India, in 1946 to study textile manufacturing. 'Eighty years ago, a young man traveled thousands of miles from India to Raleigh with little more than hope and determination,' he told the crowd. Earlier this year, he and Marilyn Kochhar also established three endowments supporting students, faculty, and college leadership at the Wilson College of Textiles.

What to watch: NC State did not immediately have an estimate of the gift's total value, and says calculations are still underway. Watch for the final dollar figure — and whether other alumni across American universities follow this model of commencement-day debt relief.
nri_angle: Kochhar's act of giving — rooted in his father's 1946 journey from Punjab to North Carolina — is a powerful reminder that the Indian immigrant story in America is still generating generational dividends, and Indian Americans who support higher education philanthropy have a new benchmark to look to.
author: Diaspora Desk
